claim: Quantization noise (NVFP4, MXFP4, NF4) inherently increases the sampling/policy entropy of an LLM's output token distribution relative to its 16-bit counterpart, functioning as an implicit exploration mechanism during RL training.
scope_conditions: Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, GRPO/DAPO RL training on GSM8K and MATH500 reasoning tasks; entropy measured during RL rollouts, not zero-shot text-generation diversity
quoted_support: We discover that quantization inherently increases the sampling entropy, H(pi(.|q)) = -sum_{o_t in V} pi(o_t|q) log pi(o_t|q), of the policy during deployment... The noise introduced by quantization serves as an implicit exploration mechanism, similar to explicit noise injection techniques in the parameter and action space.

claim: This RL-entropy finding directly contrasts with prior supervised-fine-tuning (SFT) literature showing quantization degrades training effectiveness, implying the entropy-boosting effect of quantization noise is specific to the RL training regime and does not generalize to SFT or zero-shot inference settings.
stance_target: generalizability of quantization's entropy-boosting effect beyond RL training
quoted_support: This challenges the conventional view in SFT that quantization degrades training effectiveness (Dettmers et al., 2023a; Guo et al., 2023)... This finding contrasts with results from SFT of LLMs (Dettmers et al., 2023a; Guo et al., 2023), demonstrating that controllable quantization noise in RL enhances exploration.

claim: Among the three 4-bit formats tested, NF4 (the format used in QLoRA/bitsandbytes-style quantization) shows weaker reward growth than NVFP4 and MXFP4, and NF4-based QLoRA slows inference rollout speed by 1.5-2x due to lookup-table dequantization overhead.
stance_target: NF4 quantization's relative performance/behavior compared to other 4-bit formats
quoted_support: Also, NVFP4 and MXFP4 both show better reward growth than NF4... using QLoRA (Dettmers et al., 2023a) in RL slows rollouts by 1.5-2x, further reducing efficiency. This slowdown occurs because QLoRA relies on NormalFloat 4-bit (NF4) precision, which requires unpacking and mapping to floating-point values via a lookup table before matrix multiplication.
